knowledge_point.title: Interpreting the Derivative of a Function

question.:question/problem: Consider a circle such that the radius $r$ can vary. If $A$ is the area of the circle, what is the best interpretation of $A^{′}(r)$?
question.:question/worked-solution:
The function $A(r)$ gives the area of a circle with radius $r.$ So

$$
A^{′}(r)=\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}r}=\frac{\text{Change in }A}{\text{Change in }r}.
$$

Therefore, $A^{′}(r)$ is the rate at which the area changes as the radius changes.

:answer-field/choices.:answer/value: The length of the radius of the circle
The rate at which the radius changes as the area changes
The area of a circle with radius $r$
The rate at which the area changes as the radius changes
The circumference of the circle
